### The four current Companies will get migrated to Entities. If the Portfolio Entity is not a Company, I just used other. Helper fields are going to be tricky. As they can have layered logic and be derived from other fields. For example, "Deal Size Range" is a helper field that categorizes the "Deal Size" field into ranges (e.g., Small, Medium, Large). The logic for categorizing deal sizes may change over time, and it may depend on other factors such as industry or geography. In an entropic schema, we can store the raw "Deal Size" value and the derived "Deal Size Range" value without enforcing a rigid schema. This allows us to evolve the categorization logic without needing to alter the underlying data structure.
### FEATURE TABLE Creating Features that can be turned on and off allows beta testers to opt in to new functionality without affecting the entire user base. This is especially important in an entropic schema where new fields and features may be added frequently. By gating new features behind a feature flag, we can test them with a subset of users, gather feedback, and iterate before rolling them out to everyone. This approach also allows us to manage the complexity of the evolving schema by controlling which features are active at any given time. Features are usually associated with a specific release or set of functionality, and they can be toggled on or off for different user segments (e.g., internal testers, beta users, general release). This way, we can ensure a smoother rollout and better user experience as the schema evolves. Simple refactor to remove the flag after the beta period ends and the feature is fully rolled out.
